name: Darwin Waterfront
note: Harbourside precinct (Darwin Wharf Precinct on Wikivoyage, site of the 1942 bombing) with a wave lagoon and recreation lagoon, restaurants and the Esplanade; Wikivoyage and Tourism NT both name it.

name: Stokes Hill Wharf
note: Historic wharf and waterfront precinct on Darwin Harbour with restaurants and the Royal Flying Doctor Service tourist facility covering the 1942 bombing; Wikivoyage lists it under Eat, Tourism NT under see and do.

name: Oil Storage Tunnels
note: WWII heritage site: long tunnels bored into the cliff on Kitchener Drive to store oil, with historic photos inside; paid entry per Wikivoyage.

name: Fannie Bay Gaol
note: Historic museum: former Darwin prison (1883 to 1950s) walkable inside, with the gallows; free entry, Wikivoyage gives 10:30AM-4PM.

name: Burnett House
note: Heritage house at Myilly Point designed by B.C.G. Burnett for the tropical climate; Wikivoyage suggests Sunday high tea in its gardens (public access to the house itself unconfirmed).

name: Myilly Point Heritage Precinct
note: Heritage precinct of early-20th-century houses on Myilly Point overlooking the harbour; Tourism NT lists the precinct, but it is a residential street area.

name: Brown's Mart
note: Historic 1885 stone building used as a theatre and performance venue; visitors mainly go in for shows, otherwise an exterior heritage stop.

name: Lyons Cottage
note: Historic 1925 cottage on The Esplanade built for the cable station staff, now the Indigenous tourism booking office; visitors go in to book tours.

name: Old Court House and Police Station
note: Historic colonial-era stone court and police buildings in Darwin, now NT Administrator's offices; a street-side heritage look, no public interior named.

name: Darwin Aviation Museum
note: Aviation museum about 8 km from the city with a B-52 bomber on loan from the US Air Force; Wikivoyage calls it the Aviation Heritage Centre, Tourism NT the Darwin Aviation Museum.

name: Northern Territory Parliament House
note: Territory parliament building on State Square with free public tours (booking essential per Wikivoyage); a civic building entered only on a guided tour.

name: Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory
wiki: Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory
note: Territory museum and art gallery on Bullocky Point with Aboriginal art, Cyclone Tracy and maritime galleries and the 18 ft crocodile Sweetheart; free admission per Wikivoyage.
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory

name: Darwin Military Museum
note: WWII military museum at East Point (Wikivoyage calls it the East Point Military Museum, Tourism NT the Darwin Military Museum: treat as one venue, see East Point Reserve).

name: East Point Reserve
note: Coastal reserve just north of the city with walking and cycling trails, Lake Alexander and the Darwin Military Museum; Wikivoyage suggests dawn or dusk for agile wallabies.

name: Lake Alexander
note: Artificial freshwater lake in East Point Reserve for swimming, picnics and a playground; a local recreation area, free access.

name: Bicentennial Park
note: Parkland along The Esplanade overlooking the harbour, a sunset and picnic spot; a city park with a harbour view.

name: George Brown Darwin Botanic Gardens
note: Tropical botanic gardens of 42 hectares with monsoon forest, coastal foredune and woodland walks; free entry, open 7AM-7PM per Wikivoyage.

name: Casuarina Coastal Reserve
note: Coastal reserve of about 1500 hectares with 8 km of beach below sandstone cliffs, walking paths, barbecue areas and the Old Man Rock sacred site, 20 minutes from the city.

name: Charles Darwin National Park
note: National park 4 km south-east of Darwin with WWII concrete bunkers (one a visitor centre), city lookouts, middens and fire trails; a park, but small, so a stop, not a destination.

name: Mindil Beach
note: Beach on Darwin's west coast beside the Mindil Beach Casino and sunset market, the site of the Territory Day fireworks; a beach stop, Wikivoyage names it under the sunset market.

name: Mindil Beach Sunset Market
note: Weekly night market at Mindil Beach, running on Thursdays and Sundays in the dry season only (a market running one or two days a week).

name: Parap Market
note: Weekly Saturday market at Parap, a once-a-week market (expected to fail the permanence test).

name: Nightcliff Market
note: Weekly market at Nightcliff, a once-a-week market (expected to fail the permanence test).

name: Rapid Creek Markets
note: Weekly market at Rapid Creek, a once-a-week market (expected to fail the permanence test).

name: Casuarina Beach
note: Beach section of Casuarina Coastal Reserve, with a council-designated free-beach area at its northern end; near-duplicate of Casuarina Coastal Reserve.

name: Lameroo Beach
note: Beach in Darwin's Wikipedia list of beaches; no visitor source read that names it as a stop.

name: Bundilla Beach
note: Darwin harbour-side beach, formerly Vesteys Beach and renamed Bundilla in 2021; Wikipedia only, no visitor source.

name: Wagait Beach
note: Coastal beach on the Cox Peninsula side of Darwin, listed by Tourism NT with a WWII gun emplacement.

name: Nightcliff Foreshore
note: Foreshore path and beach at Nightcliff, described by Wikipedia as one of Darwin's most popular fitness tracks; no visitor source read.

name: Lee Point
note: Beach and reserve near Casuarina, Wikipedia article only; no visitor source read naming it.

name: Holmes Jungle Nature Park
note: Nature park in Darwin's suburbs with walking trails through monsoon forest; Tourism NT lists it.

name: Leaning Tree Lagoon Nature Park
note: Nature park with a lagoon near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a local park.

name: Berry Springs Nature Park
note: Nature park about 45-50 km south of Darwin with clear spring-fed swimming pools, picnic and barbecue areas and monsoon forest walks; Wikivoyage and Tourism NT name it.

name: Howard Springs Nature Park
note: Nature park 2.9 km2 near Darwin with swimming and picnic areas; Tourism NT lists it as a nature park with swimming.

name: Gunn Point
note: Coastal headland near Howard Springs, Wikipedia article only; no visitor source read naming it as a stop.

name: Crocosaurus Cove
note: Crocodile attraction in the city centre with a crocodile cage immersion experience and crocodile displays; Wikivoyage describes it as crocodiles in the middle of the city.

name: Crocodylus Park
note: Crocodile park and zoo near Darwin Airport with more than a thousand crocodiles plus birds, primates and big cats; the Darwin Crocodile Farm, a near-duplicate name.

name: Territory Wildlife Park
note: Wildlife park at Berry Springs with monsoon and paperbark forest, a wetlands walk, an aquarium tunnel beneath a saltwater crocodile and twice-daily bird of prey shows.

name: Aquascene
note: Fish-feeding sanctuary at Doctors Gully beside the harbour where visitors feed large fish by hand, tide dependent, with a fee per Wikivoyage.

name: Batchelor Butterfly and Petting Farm
note: Butterfly farm and petting farm in Batchelor, billed by Wikivoyage as the NT's only butterfly farm, with a cafe and play area.

name: Batchelor
note: Small town at the gateway to Litchfield National Park with the Litchfield park headquarters, a butterfly farm and Batchelor Museum; a gateway town.

name: Batchelor Museum
note: Local history museum in Batchelor; Tourism NT lists it, details unread.

name: Batchelor Airfield
note: WWII airfield and anti-aircraft battery site near Batchelor with wartime remains, a heritage site rather than a visitor facility.

name: Litchfield National Park
note: National park (the destination itself, not a spot) about 1.5 hours south of Darwin: waterfalls, swimming rockholes, magnetic termite mounds, bushwalks and 4WD tracks.

name: Wangi Falls
note: Waterfall and swimming spot in Litchfield with a campground, kiosk, hot showers and barbecues; Wikivoyage calls it the park's most popular attraction.

name: Florence Falls
note: Double waterfall in monsoon forest in Litchfield with a plunge pool reached by about 160 steps; a headline swim spot.

name: Buley Rockhole
note: Series of cascading waterfalls and rockholes in Litchfield, a short walk from the car park with steps; a swimming spot.

name: Tolmer Falls
note: Waterfall in Litchfield with a viewing platform over a gorge; Tourism NT lists it as a waterfall viewing spot.

name: Magnetic Termite Mounds
note: Viewing area of magnetic termite mounds in Litchfield, the flat-faced mounds aligned north to south; a short roadside stop with a platform.

name: Tjaetaba Falls
note: Waterfall in Litchfield reached on the Greenant Creek walk, a terraced cascade; a bush walk stop.

name: Tjaynera Falls (Sandy Creek)
note: Waterfall and plunge pool at Sandy Creek in Litchfield, on a 4WD track with about a 2 km walk from the road, one of the best swims in the park per Wikivoyage.

name: Surprise Creek Falls
note: Waterfall in Litchfield named in Wikipedia's attraction list (the Wikipedia article is a Queensland falls and was not used); a campground-side falls, no visitor source read.

name: Walker Creek
note: Campground and stepped waterfalls at Walker Creek in Litchfield, the end point of Tabletop Track section 1 and start of walks.

name: The Lost City
note: Sandstone rock formations in Litchfield reached only by a 4WD track, the most challenging drive in the park per Wikivoyage.

name: Blyth Homestead
note: Historic early-20th-century cattle station homestead in Litchfield, reached by 4WD; a heritage building visitors can see.

name: Bamboo Creek Tin Mine
note: Historic tin mine site in Litchfield with mining remains; Tourism NT lists it, Wikipedia names it under sites designated for preservation.

name: Greenant Creek Walk
note: Bush walk in Litchfield to Tjaetaba Falls, listed by Tourism NT and Wikipedia; a walk route.

name: Florence Creek Walk
note: Bush walk in Litchfield along Florence Creek, listed by Tourism NT and Wikipedia; a walk route.

name: Wangi Falls Walk
note: Bush walk from Wangi Falls in Litchfield, named in Wikipedia's bushwalks list; a walk route.

name: Tabletop Track
note: Multi-day bushwalk (about 39 km, three to five days) from Wangi Falls to Florence Falls through Walker Creek, requiring a permit; a long walk route.
coordinates_source: OSM Walker Creek (approximate midpoint of the 39 km track)

name: Adelaide River
note: Small town on the Stuart Highway about 112 km south of Darwin, base for jumping crocodile river cruises, the WWII war cemetery and the Adelaide River Inn.

name: Adelaide River War Cemetery
note: WWII war cemetery with 434 military and civilian burials beside the Adelaide River, with gardens for remembrance; a war memorial site.

name: Spectacular Jumping Crocodile Cruise
note: Operator: a jumping crocodile river cruise on the Adelaide River; the place is the river (see Adelaide River), so an operator to fail.

name: Humpty Doo
note: Small rural town on the Arnhem Highway with a general store, pub and cafe, gateway to Fogg Dam and crocodile river cruises; Wikivoyage warns it is much smaller than the map suggests.

name: The Big Boxing Crocodile
note: Roadside giant sculpture of a boxing crocodile on the Arnhem Highway at Humpty Doo, one of Australia's big things, open 24/7 per Wikivoyage.

name: Fogg Dam Conservation Reserve
note: Wetland conservation reserve with bird-watching hides along a narrow road across Fogg Dam, free entry, rich birdlife per Wikivoyage.

name: Window on the Wetlands
note: Wetlands visitor park and car park on the Arnhem Highway at Middle Point (OSM); named in the region brief, not yet in a visitor source fetched, so the status is unconfirmed.
coordinates_source: OSM leisure park at Middle Point, Arnhem Highway (Nominatim)

name: Corroboree Billabong
note: Billabong in Mary River National Park with wetland wildlife cruises and fishing, a crocodile-rich billabong per Wikivoyage; the wetland is the stop, not the cruise operator.

name: Mary River National Park
note: National park of wetlands and billabongs on the Arnhem Highway, famous for dense birdlife and crocodile cruises; a park, too small to be a destination on its own, its spots are Corroboree Billabong and the wetlands.

name: Mistake Billabong
note: Billabong for wildlife viewing in the Top End, listed by Tourism NT; details and location unread.

name: Bird Billabong
note: Wetland for birdwatching in the Top End, listed by Tourism NT; details and location unread.

name: Djukbinj National Park
note: National park with wetlands, listed by Tourism NT; location within this region to be confirmed.

name: Manton Dam Recreation Area
note: Dam recreation and swimming area near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a local recreation reserve.

name: Marlow Lagoon Recreation Area
note: Recreation area with a lagoon near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a local recreation reserve.

name: Palmerston
note: Growing city about 20 km south-east of Darwin, the region's second centre, with shopping, the Palmerston Water Park and SWELL entertainment venue.

name: Palmerston Water Park
note: Water park in Palmerston, a paid water play venue listed by Tourism NT.

name: SWELL Palmerston
note: Entertainment venue in Palmerston listed by Tourism NT; a venue (leisure complex), not a landmark.

name: Howard Springs
note: Locality north-east of Darwin named for Howard Springs Nature Park, Wikipedia only; a suburb-level place.

name: Darwin Harbour
note: Harbour with wildlife cruises from Darwin (a water body, the stop is the cruise); a harbour rather than a single place.

name: Channel Island
note: Harbour island in Darwin Harbour, home to the former Channel Island Leprosarium (Tourism NT lists it, see the next entry); a harbour island.

name: Mandorah
note: Small settlement across Darwin Harbour on the Cox Peninsula reached by ferry, Wikipedia only; no visitor source read naming a stop.

name: Cullen Bay
note: Marina precinct with waterfront dining, shops and a promenade in Darwin's north-west; Tourism NT lists the marina and foreshore.

name: Stokes Hill Lookout
note: Historic lookout above Stokes Hill Wharf with a WWII heritage site; a lookout point.

name: Couzens Lookout
note: Scenic lookout point in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a lookout.

name: Survivor's Lookout
note: WWII-era lookout site in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a heritage lookout.

name: Darwin Cenotaph
note: War memorial monument in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a minor memorial.

name: USS Peary Memorial
note: WWII naval memorial in Darwin for the destroyer sunk in the 1942 raid, listed by Tourism NT; a minor memorial.

name: Old Admiralty House
note: Historic heritage building in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; exterior heritage look.

name: Government House, Darwin
note: Official residence of the Administrator, listed by Tourism NT; not open to visitors as far as known (expected to fail).

name: Old Boab Tree in Cavenagh Street
note: Historic boab tree landmark in Cavenagh Street, Darwin; a single tree landmark.

name: State Square Banyan Tree
note: Heritage banyan tree landmark on State Square beside Parliament House, listed by Tourism NT.

name: Goyder's Park
note: Waterfront park in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a city park.

name: Darwin City Geotrail
note: Self-guided heritage trail through Darwin's city centre; a route, not one place.

name: Zebra Stone
note: Natural rock formation of banded stone in the Darwin surrounds, listed by Tourism NT; a roadside geology stop.

name: Brian Creek Monsoon Forest
note: Monsoon forest walking area near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT.

name: Beatrice Hill Well and Stone Fences
note: Historic well and stone fences in the Top End, listed by Tourism NT; a small heritage site.

name: Rum Jungle Mine Manager's House
note: Historic mining heritage house at the former Rum Jungle mine, listed by Tourism NT; exterior heritage site.

name: Frances Bay Explosives Complex
note: WWII explosives storage site in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a heritage site.

name: WWII Gun Emplacement Wagait Beach
note: WWII gun emplacement at Wagait Beach, listed by Tourism NT; a heritage remnant.

name: WWII Catalina Base Doctors Gully
note: WWII flying boat base site at Doctors Gully, listed by Tourism NT; a heritage remnant beside Aquascene.

name: WWII Hughes Airfield
note: WWII airfield heritage site near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; wartime remains.

name: Strauss Airfield Precinct
note: Historic wartime airfield precinct near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; wartime remains.

name: WWII Observation Post Sandy Creek
note: WWII observation post site at Sandy Creek, listed by Tourism NT; a heritage remnant.

name: Dripstone Cliffs Observation Posts
note: WWII lookout posts at the Dripstone Cliffs above the coast near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT.

name: Remnant No 6 Oil Tank Wall
note: WWII oil tank wall remnant in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a wartime remnant.

name: Wreck of B24J Liberator Bomber Milady
note: WWII Liberator bomber wreck site near Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a wreck remnant at a remote site.

name: Channel Island Leprosarium and Reefs
note: Harbour island heritage site (former leprosarium) and reefs, listed by Tourism NT; a near-duplicate of Channel Island.

name: Yarraman Territory
note: Attraction in the Darwin surrounds listed by Tourism NT; details unread.

name: Hologram Zoo Darwin
note: Hologram animal display venue in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a paid entertainment venue.

name: Aqua Park Darwin
note: Water park attraction in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a commercial entertainment venue.

name: Gecko Climb
note: Rock climbing and adventure venue in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a commercial venue.

name: Zone 3 Laser Tag
note: Laser tag game venue in Darwin, listed by Tourism NT; a commercial game venue.

name: iPlay Casuarina
note: Entertainment venue in Casuarina, listed by Tourism NT; a commercial venue.

name: Big Bus Darwin
note: Operator: hop-on sightseeing bus tour of Darwin; an operator, not a place.

name: Barramundi Adventures Darwin
note: Operator: barramundi fishing tour from Darwin; an operator, not a place.

name: Hooked On Barra
note: Operator: barramundi fishing charter from Darwin; an operator, not a place.

name: Sail Darwin
note: Operator: sailing tour on Darwin Harbour; an operator, not a place.

name: Darwin Turf Club
note: Horse racing venue at Fannie Bay, listed by Tourism NT; a venue that hosts race meetings, not a permanent visitor attraction.

name: Darwin Entertainment Centre
note: Performing arts venue on Mitchell Street with a playhouse and studio theatre; visitors attend shows (a venue, not a sight).

name: Deckchair Cinema
note: Outdoor cinema on the harbour at the Wharf Precinct, showing films nightly in the dry season (seasonal venue, a recurring screening).

name: Darwin Festival
note: Annual 18-night arts festival in August; an event, not a permanent place.

name: BASSINTHEGRASS
note: Annual music festival held at Mindil Beach in May; an event.

name: Darwin Beer Can Regatta
note: Annual July wacky race event on Mindil Beach; an event.

name: Heineken Hottest 7s
note: Annual rugby sevens tournament in Darwin; an event.

name: Darwin Street Art Festival
note: Annual street art festival in Darwin; an event.

name: Aboriginal Art Awards
note: Annual national Indigenous art award held in Darwin, August to October; an event.

name: Darwin Cup Carnival
note: Annual horse racing carnival at Fannie Bay in July to August; an event.

name: Tiwi Islands Football League Grand Final
note: Annual football grand final on the Tiwi Islands in late March, with the Tiwi Art Sale; an event.

name: Tiwi Islands
note: Island group about 80 km north of Darwin (Bathurst and Melville islands and nine smaller islands): rainforest, beaches, Tiwi art and a Catholic mission heritage; reached by air or ferry on an organised tour.

name: Patakijiyali Museum
note: Museum at Wurrumiyanga on Bathurst Island with Tiwi history and art, Monday to Friday 9AM-2PM per Wikivoyage.

name: Wurrumiyanga Catholic Church Precinct
note: Church precinct at Wurrumiyanga on Bathurst Island, listed by Tourism NT; a church, exterior.

name: Pirlangimpi
note: Community on Melville Island (Garden Point), Wikipedia only; a settlement visited on tours, not a stop in itself.

name: Jilamara Arts and Crafts
note: Tiwi art centre on Melville Island where visitors meet artists and buy art, named in a Tourism NT article summary (not fetched); a venue selling art.

name: Tiwi by Designs
note: Tiwi art centre and shop where visitors meet artists, named in a Tourism NT article summary (not fetched); a shop-venue.

name: Garig Gunak Barlu National Park
note: National park covering the Cobourg Peninsula and nearshore islands, remote with access by permit or tour, pristine wilderness and marine turtles; the park is the destination. Parks and Wildlife NT page blocked to scripts.

name: Cobourg Peninsula
note: Peninsula of about 2100 km2 350 km east of Darwin, the same land as Garig Gunak Barlu National Park (overlaps with the park entry); remote wildlife reserve.

name: Victoria Settlement
note: Ruins of the 1838-1849 British military settlement at Port Essington on Cobourg Peninsula, reached by boat or tour; a historic site.

name: Cape Don Lighthouse
note: 1915 lighthouse at the western tip of the Cobourg Peninsula, remote and accessed by permit or tour; a lighthouse.

name: Smith Point
note: Ngardimardi camping area on the Cobourg Peninsula, Wikipedia listing only; a campground.

name: Black Point
note: Algarlalgari ranger station on the Cobourg Peninsula, Wikipedia listing only; a ranger station.

name: Dundee Beach
note: Fishing locality on Fog Bay about 59 km south-west of Darwin; Wikipedia says tourism and fishing are the draw, no visitor source read.

name: Fog Bay
note: Bay on the coast south-west of Darwin known for barramundi fishing; Wikipedia redirects it to Dundee Beach, so the bay is covered by the Dundee Beach entry.

name: Darwin Harbour Islands
note: Collective name for the islands in Darwin Harbour (Channel Island among them); a grouping, not one place.
